questions.question: Lui Ngai Ni is a festival that is associated with which of the following states?

• **Lui Ngai Ni** is a seed-sowing festival celebrated by the** Naga tribes of Manipur.**

• The festival is characterized by** traditional songs, dances, and rituals performed by the Naga communities.** It is a time for rejoicing and thanking the gods for a bountiful harvest.
 
• The festival is also an occasion for the Naga tribes to showcase their rich cultural heritage and traditional attire.

• Manipur is a state located in Northeast India, bordering Nagaland, Mizoram, and Assam. It is known for its scenic beauty, rich history, and diverse culture.

questions.question: Which Indian festival is a festival of lights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Known as the **Festival of Lights, Diwali** is one of the most popular and widely celebrated festivals in India.
 
• People celebrate by lighting **oil lamps (diyas)**, bursting firecrackers and worshiping deities like **Lakshmi** (goddess of wealth) and Lord **Ganesha**.
 
• Diwali marks the return of **Lord Rama to Ayodhya** after a 14-year exile and his victory over Ravana, according to the Ramayana.
 
• It is typically a five-day festival, with the main celebration on the third day, known as **Lakshmi Puja.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Holi** is celebrated primarily in northern India to welcome the **arrival of spring.**
 
• Holi signifies the **victory of good over evil**, particularly the burning of the demoness **Holika**.
 
• Holi falls on the **Purnima (full moon) day of the Hindu calendar month of Phalguna**, which usually occurs in March.
 
• There are **three types of Bihu celebrated in Assam**:
 
 
• **Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu)**: Celebrates the Assamese New Year and is a spring festival.
 
• **Kongali Bihu (Kati Bihu)**: A quieter festival, focused on prayer and lighting of lamps during the month of Kati.
 
• **Bhogali Bihu (Magh Bihu):** Celebrated in January to mark the end of the harvesting season.
 
 
 
• **Onam** is the **biggest festival in Kerala** and celebrates the legendary return of **King Mahabali.**
 
• One of the major attractions during Onam is the famous **snake boat races**, particularly in the** Pampa River**.
 
• Onam falls in the **Malayalam month of Chingam**, which usually occurs in August-September.

questions.question: Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. It is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of the monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. **

 
 
• **It is celebrated in Odisha**.
 
• The second day of the festival signifies the beginning of the solar month of Mithuna, during which the season of rains starts.
 
• It falls in mid-June, the first day is called Pahili Raja, the second day is Mithuna Sankranti, the third day is Bhudaaha or Basi Raja.
 
• The final fourth day is called Basumati snana, in which the ladies bathe the grinding stone as a symbol of Bhumi with turmeric paste and adore with flower, sindoor, etc.
 
• All types of seasonal fruits are offered to** mother Bhumi**.
 
• The day before the first day is called Sajabaja or preparatory day during which the house, kitchen including grinding stones are cleaned, spices are ground for three days.
 
• During these three days, women and girls take a rest from work and wear new Saree, Alata, and ornaments.
 
• It is similar to **Ambubachi Mela**.
 
• It is believed that the mother Goddess Earth or the divine wife of Lord Vishnu undergoes menstruation during the first three days.
 
• The fourth day is called Vasumati Snana, or the ceremonial bath of Bhudevi.
 
• The term Raja came from the Sanskrit word 'Rajas' which means menstruation and when a woman menstruates, she is called 'Rajaswala' or a menstruating woman, and in medieval times the festival became more popular as an agricultural holiday marking the worship of Bhudevi, who is the wife of Lord Jagannath.
 
• A silver idol of **Bhudevi **is still to be found in the Puri Temple beside Lord Jagannath.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Various festivals being celebrated across the Nations:

 
 
• Makar Sankranti: The festival of Makar Sankranti is being celebrated today when the Sun enters the Makar zodiac and the days begin to lengthen compared to nights.
 
• Pongal: In South India and particularly in Tamil Nadu, it’s the festival of Pongal which is being celebrated over 4 days at harvest time.
 
• Magha Bihu: In Assam and many parts of the North East, the festival of Magha Bihu is celebrated. It sees the first harvest of the season is offered to the gods along with prayers for peace and prosperity.
 
• Uttarayan: Gujarat celebrates it in the form of the convivial kite festival of Uttarayan.
 
• Maghi: In Punjab, Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Maghi. Bathing in a river in the early hours of Maghi is important.
 
• Saaji: In the Shimla District of Himachal Pradesh, Makara Sankranti is known as Magha Saaji. Saaji is the Pahari word for Sankranti, the start of the new month. Hence this day marks the start of the month of Magha.
 
• 
 
Kicheri: The festival is known as Kicheri in Uttar Pradesh and involves ritual bathing.

questions.question: Of which of the following states is Jallikattu a famous bull-taming festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Jallikattu**:-

 
 
• **It is a famous bull-taming festival that is celebrated in the state of Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It is a traditional sport where a bull is released into a crowd of people, and the participants try to grab and hold onto the bull's hump for as long as possible.
 
• The festival has been a part of Tamil Nadu's culture for centuries and is usually held during the Pongal festival.
 
• Jallikattu has been a controversial sport due to concerns over animal cruelty, and there have been calls to ban it.

questions.question: Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra is the cultural festival of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra **are annual festivals observed by the **Dimasa tribe**.
 
• These socio-religious events are held before the commencement of new agricultural activities.
 
• The Rabha tribe celebrates the Baikho festival during the spring season to honor and seek blessings from the goddess of wealth, 'Baikho'.
 
• During this festival, the village headman, known as the 'Kunang', conducts rituals to appease the family deity by closing the village gate on the day of worship.
 
• Subsequently, on the same night, the community participates in the 'Harni Gabra' ceremony, dedicated to worshipping the presiding deity for the well-being and protection of the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The major festivals celebrated in Assam are Bihu, Baishagu, Ali-Ai-Ligang, Baikho, Rongker, Rajini Gabra Harni Gabra, Bohaggiyo Bishu, Ambubashi Mela and Jonbill Mela and so on.
 
• The people of Assam also celebrate Holi, Durga Puja, Diwali, Swaraswati Puja, Lakshmi Puja, Kali Puja, Idd, Muharram, Me-Dam-Me-Phi, the birth and death anniversaries of Vaishnava Saints Srimanta Sankardev and Madhabdev.
 
• The tribals of Assam have their own colourful festivals like the Kherai Puja of the Bodos, the Baikhu and Pharkantis of the Rabhas, Ali-ai-ligang and Parag of the Mishing tribe, the Sagra-misawa wansawa and laghun of the Tiwas.

questions.question: Jamshedi Navroz is a festival of _________ community.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parsi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jamshedi Navroz** is celebrated by the **Parsi** community.
 
• It marks the **Persian New Year** and is celebrated with great enthusiasm among Parsis.
 
• The festival falls on the **spring equinox**, around March 21st, and symbolizes rebirth, renewal, and rejuvenation.
 
• Parsis observe this day by cleaning their homes, wearing new clothes, and preparing special meals.
 
• The celebrations often include visiting the **fire temple** to offer prayers and seek blessings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Parsi community in India is primarily concentrated in **Mumbai** and **Gujarat**.
 
• Jamshedi Navroz is named after the legendary **King Jamshed** of Persia, who is credited with starting the Parsi calendar.
 
• The festival is also known as **Nowruz** in other parts of the world, including Iran and Central Asia.
 
• It is a day for Parsis to reflect on the past year and make new resolutions for the coming year.
 
• Traditional Parsi dishes such as **patra ni machhi** (steamed fish), **ravo** (sweet semolina pudding), and **falooda** (a sweet drink) are commonly prepared for the occasion.

questions.question: Deepavali is celebrated in which month of Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kartika**__.

__
 
• Kartik (October-November):

 
 
• The Hindu calendar's eighth month, Kartik, is linked to the celebration of Deepavali (Diwali), the festival of lights.
 
• The month is also linked to the observance of Karva Chauth, a festival honoring the marriage union of husband and wife.
 
• It is also linked with festival of Bhai Dooj.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chaitra (March-April): 

 
 
• In the Hindu calendar, the first month is Chaitra and is highly fortunate.
 
• Occurs in March or April on the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The Hindu New Year, known in Maharashtra as Gudi Padwa, in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana as Ugadi, and in other parts of India as Chaitra Navratri, ushers in the month.
 
• The month is linked to fresh starts, development, and wealth as well as the start of the spring season.
 
 

 
• Ashwin (September-October): 

 
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, Ashwin, the seventh month, is connected to the celebration of Navratri, a holiday honoring the divine feminine force.
 
• Additionally, the month is linked to the celebration of Dussehra, a festival honoring Lord Rama's victory over the demon king Ravana.

questions.question: Which of the following is an animal trading festival of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vautha Mela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vautha Mela** is an **animal** **trading **festival in the Indian state of **Gujarat**.

 
 
• It is **organized **in **November **in a village called **Vautha**.
 
• Hundreds of farmers and **traders **across India **descend **on the tiny village of **Vautha **to **trade **their **decorated donkeys **and **camels **during the Vautha Fair.
 
• The fair **lasts** for **up to five days** and includes **stalls **selling **handicrafts**, **fairground rides **and incredible local fare.
 
• Camper tents are set up near the venue, providing an unmissable opportunity to witness the trading and be a part of the festivities.
 
• This time is also **religiously significant **as the **location **happens to be the **place **where **seven holy rivers unite**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Madhavpur Mela** of **Gujarat **shares its **connection **to the **Mishmi Tribe **of **Arunachal Pradesh**.

 
 
• The festival **celebrates **the **immortal journey **which **Rukmini undertook **from **Arunachal Pradesh to Gujarat** with **Lord Krishna**.
 
• The **Mishmi** **Tribe traces **its **ancestry **to the **legendary King Bhishmak **and through him to **his daughter Rukmini** and **Lord Krishna**.
 
• This event is **commemorated **by a **cultural **fair held **every year**, **commencing **on **Ram Navami**.
 
 
 
• The **Ambubachi Mela **is an **annual Mela **held at **Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati**, Assam.
 
 
• This **four-day festival** is celebrated during the **Assamese **month of **Ahaar **(**mid-June**).
 
• The Maa **Kamakhya Devi **temple is one of **Assam’s **most** well-known temples**, and **Goddess Kamakhya is worshipped here**. 
 
• It is **believed **that this **festival **is **celebrated **to **mark **the **yearly menstruation **course of **Goddess Kamakhya**.
 
 
 
• **Kumbh Mela** is a major **pilgrimage **and **festival **in **Hinduism**.
 
 
• It is celebrated in a **cycle **of approximately **12 years**, to celebrate every **revolution Brihaspati (**Jupiter) completes, at **four river-bank pilgrimage sites**: the (**Prayagraj **(Ganges-Yamuna-Sarasvati rivers confluence), **Haridwar** (Ganges),** Nashik **(Godavari), and **Ujjain** (Shipra).
 
• The **festival **is **traditionally credited **to the 8th-century Hindu philosopher and saint **Adi Shankara**, as a part of his efforts to start major Hindu gatherings for philosophical discussions and debates along with Hindu monasteries

questions.question: Ugadi is a Telugu festival celebrated on the occasion of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telugu new year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ugadi

 
 
• Ugadi, which is observed as Andhra Pradesh's Hindus' New Year's Day, is observed on the first day of the Hindu Luni-Solar Calendar in the month of Chaitra.
 
• According to the Gregorian calendar, it takes place in either March or April.
 
• This Indian holiday heralds the arrival of pleasure, joy, hope, and light.
 
• The Sanskrit words "Yuga," which means age, and "adi," which means the beginning, are combined to form the word "Ugadi."
 
• It denotes the start of a new era in plain terms.
 
• In Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana, this holiday is celebrated with great zeal and passion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ninth month of the Hindu calendar is Agrahya or Mrga.
 
• The Hindu month of Vaisakha corresponds to April or May on the Gregorian calendar in the national calendar of India.
 
• The fifth month of the Hindu calendar is shravan.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• The Chethiagiri Vihar festival is indeed a **Buddhist festival**.
 
• The festival is held at **Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• During the festival, **relics of Sariputta and Maha Moggallana** are worshipped.
 
• This festival is an important event for Buddhists, attracting many pilgrims to Sanchi.

• Sanchi is a small village in the Raisen District of the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It is famous for its Buddhist stupas, especially the Great Stupa which is one of the oldest stone structures in India.
 
• Sanchi was a major Buddhist center in India, dating back to the 3rd century BCE, commissioned by Emperor Ashoka.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism:**
 
 
• Buddhism is a religion and philosophy that developed from the teachings of the Buddha (Sanskrit: "Awakened One"), a teacher who lived in northern India between the mid-6th and mid-4th centuries BCE.
 
• Buddhism spread throughout Asia and is now a global religion.
 
• The core beliefs include the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.
 
 
 
• **Sariputta and Maha Moggallana:**
 
 
• Sariputta and Maha Moggallana were two of the most important disciples of the Buddha.
 
• They are often depicted as the Buddha's chief attendants and are revered for their great wisdom and spiritual powers.
 
• Their relics are considered sacred and are venerated by Buddhists around the world.
